skill.name: ios-application-dev
skill.description: Guides iOS app development with UIKit, SnapKit, and SwiftUI. Covers layout, navigation, accessibility, Dynamic Type, Dark Mode, privacy permissions, system integration, Metal shaders, and Swift coding standards.
skill.summary: Build and review iOS interfaces with UIKit, SwiftUI, accessibility, and Apple platform conventions.
skill.author: MiniMax-AI

content.value_statement: iOS teams need consistent guidance for layouts, navigation, accessibility, and Swift code quality. This skill provides practical UIKit, SwiftUI, and Apple platform patterns for design and review.
actual_capabilities: Choose UIKit and SwiftUI components for common app flows.
Apply touch target, safe area, 8pt grid, and responsive layout guidance.
Review Dynamic Type, Dark Mode, VoiceOver, Reduce Motion, and contrast support.
Plan navigation patterns, modal presentations, search, lists, grids, and context menus.
Use Swift coding standards for optionals, protocols, concurrency, ARC, and error handling.
Reference system integration patterns for permissions, location, sharing, lifecycle, and haptics.
limitations: Does not run Xcode builds, simulators, or automated tests by itself.
Does not replace Apple documentation for final App Store or platform policy decisions.
Examples may need adaptation for each app architecture and minimum iOS version.
Does not provide production assets, backend services, or full project scaffolding.

use_cases.title: Design a New iOS Screen
use_cases.description: Plan layout, navigation, touch targets, Dark Mode, Dynamic Type, and privacy prompts before implementation.

use_cases.title: Review a Swift Pull Request
use_cases.description: Check Swift code, UIKit or SwiftUI choices, accessibility support, and platform behavior before merge.

use_cases.title: Modernize App Patterns
use_cases.description: Update legacy screens with current SwiftUI, UIKit, system integration, and Apple interface conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Create an iOS Screen Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this screen concept for iOS layout, navigation, Dynamic Type, Dark Mode, accessibility, and privacy requirements: [describe screen].

prompt_templates.title: Choose UIKit or SwiftUI Components
prompt_templates.prompt: Given this workflow, recommend UIKit and SwiftUI components, navigation patterns, and permission timing: [workflow details].

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Swift Implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this iOS implementation for Swift coding standards, memory management, async patterns, accessibility, and Apple platform conventions: [implementation summary].

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Multi-Screen App Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an implementation plan for this multi-screen iOS app using UIKit, SwiftUI, navigation state, system integrations, and review checkpoints: [app requirements].

output_examples.input: A developer asks whether a profile editor should use a sheet, push navigation, or tabs.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: use push navigation for durable profile edits. Reserve a sheet for short focused tasks, and keep tabs for top-level sections.

output_examples.input: A team requests an accessibility review of a checkout screen.
output_examples.output: Findings include missing VoiceOver labels, small tap targets, weak contrast, and animation that needs a reduced-motion alternative.

output_examples.input: A reviewer asks how to handle location permission in a map feature.
output_examples.output: Guidance: explain value before the system prompt, request permission only in context, support denial, and avoid blocking unrelated features.

best_practices: Start with Apple platform components before creating custom controls.
Review accessibility, Dynamic Type, Dark Mode, and privacy during design.
Keep examples aligned with the app minimum iOS version and architecture.
anti_patterns: Using custom navigation that breaks back gestures or hides common iOS affordances.
Hardcoding sizes, colors, or text styles that fail Dynamic Type and Dark Mode.
Requesting permissions at launch without explaining the feature value.

faq.question: Does this skill write complete iOS apps?
faq.answer: It helps plan and review iOS implementation. Full apps still require project setup, coding, testing, and signing.

faq.question: Can it help with both UIKit and SwiftUI?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for UIKit, SnapKit, SwiftUI, navigation, layout, and common platform components.

faq.question: Does it execute commands or access external services?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation guidance and examples; execution depends on the host agent and user-approved tools.

faq.question: Can it replace Apple Human Interface Guidelines?
faq.answer: No. Use it as a practical companion, and verify final platform decisions with current Apple documentation.

faq.question: Is it useful for accessibility reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers VoiceOver labels, Dynamic Type, Reduce Motion, contrast, reading order, and touch targets.

faq.question: Can it handle older iOS versions?
faq.answer: It can note compatibility concerns, but developers must verify APIs against their deployment target.
